questions.q: An industry that processes bulky raw materials which lose much weight during manufacture is best located near the source of the raw materials mainly because
options: labour is always cheaper in rural areas
transporting the raw materials to a distant factory would be very costly
the finished product is more bulky than the raw material
questions.explanation: Bulky raw materials that lose much weight after processing are expensive to transport long distances, so locating the factory near the raw-material source reduces costs. A perishable finished product would instead favour a location near the market, not the raw-material source.

questions.q: Recycling scrap aluminium is economically important to Nigerian industries mainly because it
options: increases the need to import bauxite
provides a cheap raw material for cement manufacture
prevents the use of aluminium in making cooking utensils
reduces the amount of energy needed to produce aluminium from bauxite
questions.explanation: Recycling scrap aluminium uses far less energy than extracting and smelting aluminium from bauxite, so it lowers production costs. This is not about increasing bauxite imports or supplying cement factories; those describe different raw materials and uses.

questions.q: In a local government area in Ogun State, 60 infants under one year died out of 4,000 live births in a year. What was the infant mortality rate per 1,000 live births?
questions.explanation: The infant mortality rate is calculated as (60 ÷ 4,000) × 1,000 = 15 deaths per 1,000 live births. The figure 67 would result from dividing 4,000 by 60 instead of using the correct ratio.

questions.q: The lower temperature recorded at Jos during the hot season compared with Makurdi at a similar latitude is mainly due to Jos's
options: greater cloud cover throughout the year
questions.explanation: Temperature generally decreases with increasing altitude, and Jos lies on a high plateau while Makurdi is much lower. Proximity to the coast or distance from the Niger River does not explain the marked temperature difference.

questions.q: Which Nigerian town is most representative of the Sudan savanna vegetation belt?
questions.explanation: Kano lies in the northern part of Nigeria where the vegetation is typically Sudan savanna, with short grasses and scattered trees. Port Harcourt lies in the rainforest belt, while Ibadan and Enugu are in the derived savanna/forest transition zone.

questions.q: The establishment of a new university and a major market in a city encourages rural dwellers to move there. In population studies, this influence is best described as
questions.explanation: A pull factor attracts people to a destination, and a new university and major market provide opportunities that draw rural dwellers into the city. A push factor would instead be an unpleasant condition at the place of origin, such as land shortage or poor rural services.

questions.q: Rapid population growth in many Nigerian cities often results in
options: a reduction in the number of new houses needed
a fall in the demand for social services
a rise in per capita farmland in the city
pressure on housing, water supply and transport
questions.explanation: When urban population grows faster than services and infrastructure, housing, water supply and transport become overstretched. Farmland per person does not rise in crowded cities, and the need for new houses increases rather than falls.

questions.q: A farmer in Kebbi State plans to sow millet on a 2.5-hectare farm at a seed rate of 20 kg per hectare. What quantity of millet seed is required?
questions.explanation: The seed needed is the seed rate multiplied by the area: 20 kg/ha × 2.5 ha = 50 kg. The value 22.5 kg would result from adding the rate and area instead of multiplying them.

questions.q: The growing of one crop over a large area for sale, usually with processing on the estate, is best described as
questions.explanation: Plantation agriculture involves large estates, usually growing one crop for sale, and often processing the crop before export. Shifting cultivation and bush fallowing are mainly subsistence systems that involve resting land, while mixed cropping combines several crops.

questions.q: A farmer in Bauchi State notices declining maize yields despite yearly application of NPK fertilizer. Which practice will most directly improve the organic matter content of the soil?
options: incorporating compost or farmyard manure into the soil
planting maize continuously without a cover crop
questions.explanation: Compost and farmyard manure add organic matter directly, improving soil structure, water retention and nutrient supply. NPK fertilizer supplies mineral nutrients but does not restore organic matter, and burning residues destroys the organic material that could have been incorporated.

questions.q: The main difficulty in exploiting timber in the tropical rainforest of southern Nigeria is that valuable tree species...
options: lose their leaves for most of the year
grow only on steep, inaccessible hills
are widely scattered among many other species
have very soft wood that decays quickly
questions.explanation: Commercial timber trees occur in mixed stands, so selective logging is costly and difficult. They are not confined to steep hills, and the rainforest is evergreen rather than mostly leafless.

questions.q: Bauxite is mined in Nigeria mainly for the extraction of...
questions.explanation: Bauxite is the principal ore from which aluminium is refined. Tin comes mainly from cassiterite, iron from hematite or magnetite, and lead from galena.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The part of the Earth’s interior that is believed to be liquid because S-waves cannot pass through it is the...
questions.explanation: S-waves do not travel through liquids, and their disappearance beyond the outer core indicates that this layer is liquid. The inner core is solid, while the mantle and crust are mainly solid.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: An observer at latitude 20°N sees the Pole Star. The star appears...
questions.explanation: The altitude of the Pole Star above the horizon is approximately equal to the observer’s latitude, so at 20°N it is about 20° above the northern horizon. It is not at 70° or overhead, and it is not seen above the southern horizon from that latitude.

questions.q: Which mode of transport is most suitable for moving large tonnages of iron ore over a long inland distance from Itakpe to Warri?
questions.explanation: Rail transport is best suited to bulky goods over long inland distances because it can carry large tonnages economically. Road transport is less efficient for such heavy consignments, air transport is too costly and limited, and pipelines are used mainly for fluids or gases.

questions.q: A Nigerian insurance company provides cover for a shipping firm based in Ghana and is paid in dollars. This transaction is an example of Nigeria’s...
questions.explanation: The sale of a service, such as insurance, to a foreign firm earns foreign exchange and is an invisible export. Visible exports are physical goods, while an invisible import is a service purchased from abroad.

questions.q: The distance between two villages on a map with scale 1:25,000 is 7.2 cm. A road is to be constructed between them at a cost of ₦18 million per kilometre. What is the total cost of the road?
questions.explanation: The ground distance is 7.2 × 25,000 = 180,000 cm, which equals 1.8 km. The cost is therefore 1.8 × ₦18 million = ₦32.4 million.

questions.q: The sideways widening of a river valley by erosion is mainly due to
questions.explanation: Lateral erosion attacks the sides and banks of a river channel, causing the valley to widen. Vertical erosion deepens the channel, while headward erosion extends the valley upstream.

questions.q: A river capture occurs when
options: a vigorously eroding river cuts back and diverts the headwaters of a weaker neighbouring river
a river deposits its load where its gradient decreases
a meander is cut off to form an ox-bow lake
a river flows underground through limestone openings
questions.explanation: River capture results from strong headward erosion by one river, which breaches the divide and diverts the upper course of another river. Deposition on a gentler gradient produces features such as alluvial fans, not river capture.

questions.q: A mechanic village in Lagos has large quantities of used lead-acid batteries. Which measure best reduces the danger to people and the environment?
options: Burning them in the open to recover the metal
Pouring their acid content into a nearby drainage channel
Burying them in an unlined pit at the edge of the village
Collecting the batteries for treatment in licensed recycling facilities
questions.explanation: Lead-acid batteries contain lead and corrosive acid, so controlled collection and licensed recycling reduce soil, water and air contamination. Burying, pouring out the acid or open burning would release toxic substances into the environment.

questions.q: A steep slope in Anambra State is becoming unstable after heavy rain because vegetation has been cleared. Which practice is most likely to reduce the risk of landslide?
options: Redirecting roof runoff directly onto the slope
Building more houses at the foot of the slope
Removing remaining topsoil to expose the bedrock
Planting deep-rooted trees and constructing drainage channels on the slope
questions.explanation: Tree roots help bind the soil, and drainage channels reduce water infiltration and pore pressure, lowering landslide risk. Adding buildings, exposing bedrock or concentrating runoff on the slope would make the slope less stable.

questions.q: A parcel of air at sea level has a temperature of 24°C. It rises to a height of 1,500 m and cools at 0.6°C per 100 m. Assuming no condensation occurs, what is its temperature at 1,500 m?
questions.explanation: The air rises through 1,500/100 = 15 hundred-metre layers. The total cooling is 15 × 0.6°C = 9°C, so the final temperature is 24°C − 9°C = 15°C. The value 33°C would result from adding the cooling instead of subtracting it.

questions.q: A place on longitude 75°E records a local solar time of 16:20. What is Greenwich Mean Time?
questions.explanation: Longitude 75°E is 75 ÷ 15 = 5 hours ahead of Greenwich. GMT is therefore 16:20 − 5:00 = 11:20. Adding the difference instead gives 21:20, which reverses the direction from Greenwich.

questions.q: On 21 June, the noon Sun is directly overhead at about 23.5°N. What is the altitude of the noon Sun at a place on latitude 10°N?
questions.explanation: At local noon the solar altitude is 90° minus the difference between the Sun’s declination and the observer’s latitude. Here the difference is 23.5° − 10° = 13.5°, so the altitude is 90° − 13.5° = 76.5°. The value 56.5° is obtained by subtracting both latitudes from 90°.

questions.q: Which Nigerian town has the smallest annual variation in day length?
questions.explanation: Day length varies least near the Equator and increases towards higher latitudes. Lagos is closest to the Equator among the listed towns, so its annual range of daylight hours is the smallest.

questions.q: The growth of Nsukka in Enugu State as an urban settlement is most closely associated with the establishment of which activity?
questions.explanation: Nsukka grew notably as a university town after the University of Nigeria was established there, attracting students, staff and service activities. Coal mining is associated more with Enugu, while oil and tin have their main centres elsewhere.

questions.q: Which site would be most suitable for an early farming settlement in a riverine area of Nigeria that experiences annual flooding?
options: A steep hilltop with no reliable water supply
The lowest part of the floodplain close to the river
A sandbar exposed only in the dry season
Slightly raised land beside the river above flood level
questions.explanation: Slightly raised ground beside a river provided fertile alluvial soil, water and a route while avoiding regular flooding. A low floodplain or dry-season sandbar would be unsafe, and a steep hilltop without reliable water would be poorly suited to farming.

questions.q: A palm oil mill is best located close to oil palm plantations mainly because
options: the mill is market-oriented because palm oil is difficult to store
the processed oil is more bulky and perishable than the fruit
the palm fruit is bulky and spoils soon after harvesting
the plantation provides a large local market for the processed oil
questions.explanation: Palm fruit must be processed soon after harvesting because it spoils quickly, and transporting bulky fruit is costly. The finished oil is less bulky and can be moved over longer distances, so the mill is located near the raw material.

questions.q: Oloibiri is historically important in Nigerian economic geography because it is the place where
options: limestone was first quarried for cement
tin was first smelted in commercial quantity
coal was first mined in commercial quantity
crude oil was first discovered in commercial quantity
questions.explanation: Oloibiri, in the Niger Delta, is remembered as the site of the first commercial crude oil discovery in Nigeria. Coal, tin and limestone are associated with other Nigerian localities and industries.

questions.q: The main cocoa-growing belt in Nigeria lies mainly in the
questions.explanation: Cocoa requires a warm, humid climate and shade, conditions found mainly in the forest zone of south-western Nigeria. The Sahel and savanna are too dry, while mangrove swamps are unsuitable for cocoa.

questions.q: In the demographic transition model, the second stage is best described by
options: birth rate falling faster than death rate to very low levels
high birth rate and high death rate
high birth rate and falling death rate
low birth rate and low death rate
questions.explanation: In the second stage, improvements in food supply, sanitation and medicine cause death rates to fall while birth rates remain high. The first stage has both birth and death rates high, while the later stages have low birth and death rates.

questions.q: A farmer at Jos grows Irish potatoes and cabbage on terraced fields. Which climatic condition of the Jos Plateau most favours these crops?
options: Cool temperatures and moderate to high rainfall
Hot, humid conditions with saline coastal air
A long dry season with high evaporation
Consistently high temperatures and low rainfall
questions.explanation: The high altitude of the Jos Plateau lowers temperatures, and the area receives moderate to high rainfall, conditions suitable for temperate crops such as Irish potatoes and cabbage. Hot, dry or saline conditions would not favour these crops.

questions.q: A cooperative in Abeokuta buys 500 bags of fertiliser at ₦18,000 per bag and sells them to members at ₦19,800 per bag. What is the total profit made by the cooperative?
questions.explanation: The profit per bag is ₦19,800 − ₦18,000 = ₦1,800. For 500 bags, total profit is 500 × ₦1,800 = ₦900,000. The value ₦9,900,000 is the total selling revenue, not the profit.

questions.q: A farmer in a dry part of Borno State wants to reduce wind erosion and conserve soil moisture. Which practice is most suitable?
options: Ploughing deeply along the direction of the prevailing wind
Removing all crop residues and keeping the soil bare
Flooding the field with saline water during the dry season
Planting shelterbelts of trees and leaving crop residues as mulch
questions.explanation: Shelterbelts reduce wind speed, while crop residues as mulch protect the soil surface and reduce evaporation. Bare soil and ploughing along the wind direction expose the field to more erosion, and saline water can damage the soil.

questions.q: In the equatorial rainforest belt of Nigeria, the forest floor is usually sparsely covered with small plants mainly because
options: the trees shed all their leaves in the dry season
little sunlight penetrates the dense canopy
the area receives very little rainfall
questions.explanation: Tall trees form a dense upper canopy that blocks most sunlight from reaching the forest floor, so undergrowth is limited. The equatorial rainforest has high rainfall and evergreen trees, not permanently frozen soil or complete dry-season leaf fall.

questions.q: Which soil particle size has the greatest ability to hold water and nutrients because of its very small pore spaces?
questions.explanation: Clay particles are extremely fine and have a large surface area, enabling them to retain much water and many nutrients. Coarse sand and gravel drain rapidly, while silt is intermediate but holds less than clay.

questions.q: Which sequence best explains how an igneous rock can be changed into a sedimentary rock?
options: Evaporation of water and crystallisation of salts
Weathering, transportation, deposition and compaction with cementation
Subjection to heat and pressure only
questions.explanation: An igneous rock first breaks down by weathering, and the fragments are transported and deposited before being compacted and cemented into a sedimentary rock. Melting and cooling would form igneous rock, while heat and pressure alone would produce metamorphic rock.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which planet is tilted on its axis at about 98°, so that it appears to roll along its orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an axial tilt of about 98°, so its rotation is almost in the plane of its orbit and it appears to roll along that orbit. Venus is noted for retrograde rotation, but it does not have the extreme rolling tilt described.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The Earth is farthest from the Sun at a point in its orbit called the
questions.explanation: The point in Earth's orbit farthest from the Sun is called aphelion, while the nearest point is perihelion. Solstices and equinoxes describe particular positions in the yearly cycle, not the farthest orbital point.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: A leap year has 366 days mainly because the Earth takes about
options: 365 days to complete one revolution around the Sun
365¼ days to complete one revolution around the Sun
27⅓ days to revolve around the Sun
24 hours to rotate once on its axis
questions.explanation: A tropical year is about 365¼ days, so an extra day is added to February almost every four years to keep the calendar in step. The alternative of 24 hours describes one rotation, not one revolution.
